correctness.rationale: Every distance-two clique of L(G) either is an original edge star (triangle-free argument) or has disjoint edges a,b with unique connector c. For each third edge f the union of three short line-graph walks involves at most six G-edges, and hence is a tree at girth >=7. The tree midpoint inequality forces f to meet c, proving Rips2=Cech2. The complete uniquely-centered face-toggle matching then gives genuine elementary collapses to Cl(L(G)); the star nerve is G. The C6 boundary is computed exactly. Included verifier exhaustively replays 1467 finite cases but is not substituted for the infinite argument.

originality.rationale: The only directly dominating-looking prior result establishes a Čech nerve collapse for line graphs with no 3- or 4-cycles. The new claim additionally proves the precise Rips2=Cech2 coincidence in girth at least seven using a six-edge tree-midpoint lemma, and hence gives a simplicial Rips2-to-Rips1 collapse. The distinction is substantive: C6 satisfies the preceding Cech theorem yet the corresponding Rips and Cech complexes differ, and the Rips persistence changes dimensions. The primary published line-graph result covers only scale-one cliques. published-finding corpus and own-claim comparisons found no encompassing Rips counterpart, subject to unindexed-work risk.

value.rationale: This establishes a sharp, infinite-family simple-homotopy persistence stability law for the Rips filtration of all line graphs of girth-seven graphs, even with arbitrary degree and branching. It identifies a concrete structural cause (six-edge acyclic midpoint Helly behavior) for equality of Rips and Čech, a distinction not obtained from known Čech homotopy and scale-one line-graph results. At girth six this stability fails in homotopy dimension, demonstrating a motivated exact boundary rather than a routine numerical special case.
